actions.visual_identity_evidence: Similar landscapes hang on opposite end walls: shot1 beside the bookcase, shot3 beside the hallway console; the 5.57-unit separation supports this topology. Relocation of the whole arrangement is unsupported by the frames and conflicts with p07–p09; repeated artwork alone cannot establish identity.

Shot3's cropped leaves beside the bookcase do not reveal the shelf level, pot or trailing form needed to identify shot1's shelf plant; 4.79-unit separation raises doubt but cannot resolve identity with this crop and inaccurate fit.

The narrow corner table and wider doorway-wall console have different wall/window relationships and top arrangements; 4.36-unit separation corroborates distinct locations. Perspective affects width but cannot explain the opposite-wall topology, and p07 supplies no relocation event.

Independently reconsidered after rejecting the tables: the compact fine-stemmed corner plant and broad dense cascading console plant occupy opposite-wall arrangements. Foliage drift alone is insufficient, but their distinct placement and no transfer evidence under p07 support different instances over relocation or depth error.

Similar gold-framed landscapes occupy opposite end walls: A beside the bookcase, B beside the hallway doorway; their tree/water compositions also differ. The 5.57-unit separation corroborates this topology, rather than proving it; relocation conflicts with p02/p07 and lacks visual support.

B exposes only foliage beside a cropped dark cabinet; shelf height, pot and trailing structure cannot be verified against A. The 4.79-unit separation raises doubt but neither distinguishes another plant nor proves relocation.

A's compact table has a short front and narrow footprint; B shows a broad console with a long drawer front beside the hallway. Opposite-wall context and differing construction support separate furniture, beyond the 4.36-unit separation; p07 provides no relocation explanation.

Independently of the rejected tables, A's visible crown is small and sparse while B has a broad dense crown and multiple long hanging strands; opposite-wall supports corroborate separate plants. Occlusion affects height estimates, but does not explain the crown structure; relocation plus growth/change lacks support under p07.

The first landscape is on the end wall beside the bookcase, whereas the reverse view places its landscape beside the entrance, at the opposite end of the window wall. Similar landscape imagery cannot override this structural distinction. The 5.57-unit separation supports the check, not the decision; p02/p07 provide no painting relocation, and p08/p09 explain the reversed view. Reject g01 as an anchor.

Reverse-view edge foliage lacks a complete pot, trailing pattern and verified shelf level. Its 4.79-unit offset and lower apparent placement challenge identity, but cropping and fit error prevent distinguishing a separate plant from relocation or the same shelf plant; p07 alone cannot resolve this.

The narrow table stands beyond the curtain toward the bookcase-side end; the reverse-view broad console stands by the entrance on the opposite end wall. The 4.36-unit separation is consistent with those locations; partial first-shot geometry alone is insufficient, but the room layout and p02/p07 favor separate tables over relocation.

Independently of the rejected support match, the first plant has a small sparse crown and finer short visible trails; the entrance-console plant has a broad dense crown and heavy long cascade. Occlusion limits height comparison, but opposite-wall placement, these visible differences and p02/p07 support distinct plants rather than an undocumented transfer; 4.35-unit separation is corroborative only.

Doorway context places the similar tapered pots at opposite ends: television-side in shot1 and sofa-side in shot3. This independently supports the 6.37-unit separation; no distinctive pot marking or observed transfer supports relocation, and the prompt preserves non-cup locations.

Independent foliage review places the flower clusters outside opposite doorway ends; generic leaves and flowers supply no individual identifier. The 7.28-unit separation agrees with that context, while neither visible handling nor the prompt supports transferring this plant.

Shot1's panel borders the television wall, whereas shot3's panel borders the sofa-and-lamp wall: opposite jambs under the reversed view. Repeated fabric does not identify one panel; the 4.27-unit separation corroborates context, and fixed hanging panels plus the unchanged-room prompt favor different instances over relocation or depth error.

Door-jamb context places the pots at opposite ends of the opening: television-side in shot1 and sofa-side in shot3. The 6.37-unit separation prompts this check but does not decide it; generic tapered pots provide no distinctive relocation evidence, and the prompt preserves all non-cup locations.

Independent inspection places each flowering crown above a different jamb-side pot; similar sparse foliage and flowers supply no unique identity bridge. The 7.28-unit separation is consistent with those locations, while neither a transplant nor whole-pot relocation is visually supported or specified.

Matching fabric belongs to opposite doorway panels: shot1 adjoins the television wall, shot3 the sofa/lamp corner. Reverse viewing does not interchange these physical jambs. The 4.27-unit offset corroborates this context; no panel transfer is shown, the prompt preserves curtains, and g17 is rejected as an anchor.

Both cameras remain indoors: the first pot is beyond the television-side jamb, the second beyond the sofa-side jamb. Similar tapered pots do not override these opposite structural locations; the 6.37-unit separation corroborates rather than establishes the split. Global/shot3 preserve other props, and no distinctive mark or transport supports relocation.

Independently of pot identity, the foliage clusters occupy opposite doorway-side exterior positions and lack distinctive matching branches or blooms. Their 7.28-unit separation alone is insufficient, but the jamb context and global/shot3 unchanged planting favor different instances over unsupported relocation.

The television-side panel and sofa/lamp-side panel flank different doorway jambs; looking toward the garden from indoors does not exchange those physical supports. Repeated fabric is insufficient, and global/shot3 preserve curtains rather than rehang them. The 4.27-unit separation supports this visual distinction despite fit error; reject anchor g17.

The similar landscapes occupy opposite background walls: A beside the bookcase, B above the console beside the entrance. The 5.29-unit separation supports this structural distinction despite poor registration; shot2 excludes intervening room rearrangement, so repeated artwork does not establish relocation or identity.

A's narrow stand has a short apron and compact top; B's console has a much broader drawer front and stands on the opposite entrance-side wall. The 4.23-unit offset corroborates distinct furniture rather than deciding it; reverse perspective and A's weak reconstruction cannot explain both structure and wall context, and shot2 excludes furniture relocation.

Independently of the rejected support match, A has a compact crown and thin visible trails, while B has a wider crown and longer dense strands. The 3.99-unit offset and different walls favor separate plants, but A's limited visibility prevents individual identification; unshown relocation is unsupported by shot2, not visually impossible.

A's picture adjoins the bookcase beyond the window; B's hangs above a broad console beside the doorway on the opposite end wall. Repeated landscape imagery does not overcome these different architectural settings. The 5.29-unit separation supports this distinction; reconstruction error cannot explain the wall context, and shot2 specifies no furniture or prop rearrangement.

A shows a narrow stand between curtain and bookcase-side wall picture; B shows a broad drawer console beneath the opposite doorway-side picture. The 4.23-unit separation agrees with different wall locations and furniture proportions; A's partial geometry alone would be insufficient, while shot2 supplies no relocation event.

Independently of the rejected tables, A's compact crown and sparse hanging growth differ from B's broad crown and dense long vines in opposite wall settings. Similar round foliage is nondistinctive; the 3.99-unit offset corroborates separate instances, while occlusion explains some extent difference but supplies no evidence of plant transfer during shot2.
